quote: While APA § 10.12 (Order of Precedence) provides that the APA controls in case of conflict, relying on a precedence clause to undo an operative conveyance is litigation risk, not a substitute for clear drafting.
reason: The memo gets most of the issue right. It flags that Bill of Sale § 1.1(b) defines 'Purchased Assets' as all assets 'used or held for use in the Business' with no Excluded Assets carve-out. It names the Albany facility and the HOLLIS trademark as at risk of being conveyed. It recommends adopting the APA definition 'other than the Excluded Assets' or adding an express exclusion. However, the criterion also requires explaining that the Bill of Sale controls as to its subject matter under APA § 10.12. The memo says the opposite: that § 10.12 makes the APA control in a conflict. That misreading treats the APA as a backstop when, per the ledger, the Bill of Sale's broader definition would govern the conveyance. This understates the risk to Marrowind and gets wrong the provision the criterion relies on, so the issue is not identified correctly in substance.
